contact_edits.before: Andrew's at Hazelton Lanes hosts a special afternoon of fashion and fundraising tomorrow for the Peter Munk Cardiac Centre at Toronto General Hospital. Canadian designer Dominic Bellissimo makes a personal appearance to present his Winter 2003 shearling coats and his new home apparel shearling collection of throws, pillow and small furnishings. Champagne cocktails and cuisine will be served. Silent auction. 1 p.m. to 4 p.m. 55 Avenue Rd. 416-969-9991.

contact_edits.before: How can we miss the Eagles if they won't go away? And why would anyone pay as much as $250 to see them when they could see vulgar gender bender Peaches at the Guvernment on the same night? The band that gave us Desperado and Hotel California bring its 17th annual farewell tour to the Air Canada Centre tonight (416-870-8000), but, with apologies to Don Henley, you're much better off seeing Peaches - - the abrasive, sometimes bearded Canadian vixen of electroclash and rap. Not for the faint of heart. But then again, those with heart conditions should probably avoid the credit card bills that result from a night with the Eagles. Friday and Saturday, the critically revered Constantines play the Horseshoe (416-598-4226). But, it should be noted, future child star drug casualties Hanson play the Guvernment on Friday, while surf rock refugees Smash Mouth play the same venue Saturday. On second thought, maybe that shouldn't be noted. Forget we even mentioned it. Aaron Wherry

contact_edits.before: Perhaps a month after the Toronto International Film Festival, take comfort in the little festivals -- the kind where you show up and buy a ticket at the door; so civilized -- that crop up in this film-loving town almost every weekend. From tomorrow to Tuesday the 14th, the Royal Cinema hosts the Toronto International Latin Film Festival. Includes Spanish, Portuguese, French and Italian language films on Latin culture, and the vastness of the mandate makes for some intriguing programming. Of note: About Bunuel, a Spanish/ Mexican/ French documentary on Luis Bunuel; Three Nights of a Saturday, a black comedy set in Santiago during a pivotal soccer match; and Condor Crux: The Legend, the first full-length computer animated film to come out of Argentina. For scheduling, check www.tilff.com. Royal Cinema, 608 College St. Ticketing: 416-364- 3131. Katrina Onstad
